title: The spies (Numbers 13–14)
hook: ten saw giants, two saw a land of milk and honey

segments.voice: Yesterday, the blessing: keeping, a shining face, mercy and peace. Your line was the lord bless thee. This week ran from the golden calf through God's back, the dwelling, be holy and the jubilee.

Twelve men come back from a forty-day scouting trip, and two of them carry a single cluster of grapes on a pole between them. That's how big the grapes are. They bring pomegranates and figs, too. The report starts well: it's a land flowing with milk and honey, just as promised. Then comes the word but. The people there are strong. The cities are great and walled. We saw giants, and next to them we were like grasshoppers, and that's how we looked to them.
screen: `TWELVE SCOUTS, FORTY DAYS.` → `GRAPES CARRIED ON A POLE.` → `BUT WE SAW GIANTS.`

segments.voice: First, two reports from one trip. All twelve saw the same fruit, the same walls, the same tall people. Ten came back saying we can't. Two, Caleb and Joshua, said we can. Caleb quiets the crowd: let's go up at once and take it, for we are well able. In Hebrew he doubles the verb, a way of insisting: we can, we surely can. Second, the grasshopper line. We were grasshoppers in our own sight, and so we were in theirs. How would they know what the giants thought? They never asked. They decided how small they were, and assumed everyone else agreed. Third, the night of weeping. The whole people cry all night. Let's choose a leader and go back to Egypt, they say, back to the bricks. Joshua and Caleb tear their clothes and plead: the land is very good; don't be afraid; the Lord is with us. And the crowd talks about stoning them. Fourth, the cost. A whole generation decides it can't, and the text takes them at their word: forty years in the wilderness, a year for each day of scouting, until that generation has passed, and of all those twenty and older who were counted, only Caleb and Joshua will walk into the land. The Church names this courage fortitude, one of the four cardinal virtues. The Catechism says it gives firmness in difficulties and constancy in pursuing the good, and that it enables a person to conquer fear. Not to feel no fear. To conquer it.
screen: `SAME LAND, TWO REPORTS.` · `GRASSHOPPERS IN OUR OWN SIGHT.` · `A NIGHT OF WEEPING FOR EGYPT.` · `FORTITUDE: TO CONQUER FEAR.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind something that feels like a giant right now, a deadline, a hard conversation, a health worry, and notice the story you're telling about yourself next to it. Then look at it the way Caleb did: same walls, same giants, but what's the fruit on the other side? If you pray, bring that fear to God and listen for Caleb's words; if not, just try on the second report.
The spies. Twelve scouts who saw the same land: ten saw giants and fear, two saw milk and honey and said we can. Today's word.
Your line: we are able. Ten saw giants; two saw the fruit. Day three hundred eighty-five.

howItsDone: The Catholic Church counts fortitude among the four cardinal virtues and among the seven gifts of the Holy Spirit given in confirmation, and the Catechism describes it as firmness in difficulty that enables a person to conquer fear.

chat.says: Why did Israel wander forty years if the land was right there?
options: After the scouts' report, the people said we can't, and the text took them at their word.
Because the scouts reported the land was poor, with no food worth having.
God wanted to wait until Caleb and Joshua were old enough to lead.
chat.meaning: Ten of the twelve scouts saw giants and said we can't. A generation decided it couldn't, and spent forty years in the wilderness.

Caleb.meaning: one of the two scouts who said we can

fortitude.meaning: courage: the virtue that helps a person conquer fear

cardinal virtues.meaning: the four virtues on which a good life turns

Catechism.meaning: the Catholic Church's official summary of its teaching

notes: Week-end look-back (379–385) carried in the review: the golden calf, God's back, the dwelling, be holy, jubilee (and the blessing as yesterday).

Caleb's words (13:30; DR 13:31 'we shall be able to conquer it') and the grasshopper line (13:33; DR 13:34 'locusts') paraphrased. Verse numbering differs between the DR and the KJV/Hebrew here. Confirm.
Yakhol nukhal (infinitive absolute + finite verb) at 13:30: confirm.
Only Caleb and Joshua of the adults twenty and up (14:29–30, 38): 'of all the adults who left Egypt'. Confirm the wording.
CCC 1808 (fortitude ... enables one to conquer fear, even fear of death) and 1831 (gifts of the Spirit). Confirm.
